Data.title: XRP Price Prediction: Whale Wallets Shrink as $61M in Tokens Moves Onto Exchanges
Data.body: Key takeaways XRP whale wallets decline from 351 to 339 Exchange balances rise by approximately 47 million XRP Losing $1.26 support could expose prices below $1 XRP is facing renewed selling concerns after the number of large-holder wallets declined and approximately $61 million worth of additional tokens appeared in exchange-associated balances. The cryptocurrency traded near $1.29 on October 26, down roughly 17% over the past month, as investors assessed whether recent whale activity could trigger another decline. According to analyst Ali Martinez , addresses holding between 10 million and 100 million XRP fell from 351 to 339 over several weeks. His October 25 analysis also identified $1.26 as a critical support level that could determine whether the correction deepens. XRP Whale Wallets Shrink as Exchange Holdings Rise The decline represents 12 fewer addresses in the 10 million–100 million XRP category, according to Santiment figures shared by Martinez. At $1.30 per token, addresses in this category hold between $13 million and $130 million in XRP. However, leaving the category does not necessarily mean an investor sold their entire position. A wallet might transfer assets to another address, split its holdings or move above the 100 million XRP threshold. Meanwhile, exchange-associated balances in Martinez's dataset increased from approximately 11.003 billion to 11.05 billion XRP, a net rise of around 47 million tokens. That represents approximately $61.1 million at the reference price. The development adds to earlier exchange inflow concerns , when 6.05 billion XRP in gross deposits were recorded over a separate 30-day period. However, gross deposits and net exchange balances are different metrics. Neither automatically proves that investors sold their XRP. An independent exchange-wallet tracker also reports different totals and changes because it follows a different set of labeled addresses, reinforcing the importance of comparing consistent datasets. Can XRP Hold $1.26 as Institutional Demand Slows? The latest whale figures arrive as XRP ETF investment shows signs of weakening. U.S. spot XRP ETFs attracted approximately $4.3 million during the October 19–23 trading week, recovering from the previous week's modest withdrawals. However, the funds recorded no net inflows on October 23, despite substantial cumulative investment since their launches. Coinpaper recently reported that XRP ETF assets were worth approximately $1.48 billion against $1.81 billion in cumulative net inflows. Meanwhile, XRP Ledger participation continues expanding. Santiment recently identified a record 8.24 million funded wallets . That contrast highlights why more wallets do not necessarily translate into higher cryptocurrency prices. For traders, the immediate question is whether XRP can hold above $1.26, the lower boundary of a price channel identified by Martinez. XRP Price Prediction: Could Whales Push XRP Below $1? Martinez warned that sustained trading below $1.26 could expose $1.11, followed by a more significant decline toward $0.98. The latter would represent approximately 22% downside from the $1.26 breakdown level, although the scenario depends on continued selling and a confirmed loss of support. Conversely, defending $1.26 and reclaiming $1.40 could strengthen the case for a recovery toward $1.50. Market sentiment may also be influenced by Ripple's October 27–29 Swell conference, where financial institutions will discuss payments, stablecoins and tokenization. Coinpaper's recent Ripple partnership analysis highlighted why institutional agreements do not automatically generate equivalent XRP demand. Traders are also monitoring Ripple's scheduled November escrow release , although unlocked tokens are not necessarily sold. For now, whale distribution remains a warning signal rather than proof of an impending crash. Whether XRP stabilizes above $1.26 will matter more than the wallet-count decline alone.

Data.title: Aviva Investors unveils $29 billion tokenized liquidity fund on XRP Ledger
Data.body: Aviva Investors has launched a new tokenized share class for the firm’s largest fund with approximately £22 billion ($29.37 billion) in assets under management, per a joint announcement made with Ripple on Monday, October 26. The launch of a new tokenized share class for the Aviva Investors Sterling (GBP) Liquidity Fund represents a significant expansion to the firm’s tokenized fund offering and has turned the company into one of the largest asset management providers to offer such a product in Europe. Furthermore, Aviva unveiled an investment of £50 million ($66 million) in this new tokenized share class. Remarking on the launch, CEO of Aviva Investors, Mark Versey, highlighted that the move represents a sign of its ‘clear intent’ to become a leader ‘in this area’ and underlined the importance of the partnership with Ripple: This expansion of our tokenised offering shows our clear intent to be a leader in this area and sets the groundwork for a future expansion of our capabilities. We believe tokenised funds can increase efficiency and ultimately lead to improved client outcomes. Our partnership with Ripple has once again been vital to our efforts, and we look forward to continuing working together, as we look to further explore the possibilities of tokenisation. Ripple’s Senior Vice President, Nigel Khakoo, expressed delight with the pace of tokenized fund launches, while emphasizing the importance of his own company and the XRP ledger in ensuring ‘compliance, privacy and security features needed by institutions.’ What is the Aviva Investors Sterling Liquidity Fund? The Sterling Liquidity Fund, for its part, was established in 2002 and is domiciled in Ireland. At its core, it invests in short-term and high-quality debt instruments denominated in sterling. Its stated goal is to provide investors with comparatively low-risk returns, while enabling daily access to the traders’ money. Notably, the new asset class uses a ‘digital twin’ structure where, rather than being transferred directly onto the blockchain, the holdings are represented digitally, and the conventional structure, as well as regulatory protections and custody arrangements, remain in place. Data.title: David Schwartz explains why banks should pick XRP over Ethereum and Solana
Data.body: David Schwartz , former CTO of Ripple, has defended the continued relevance of XRP in international finance. In the interview aired Saturday, the manager argued that banks may still have to choose XRP over Ethereum and Solana for some use cases. His comments come as rivalry among Ripple, Ethereum, and Solana continues to intensify in on-chain finance. Amid the competition, global firms favor different protocols due to core infrastructure and regulatory clarity. Ethereum, XRP, or Solana? Which is better for banks In the podcast, Schwartz said XRP can be better situated for certain use cases. He said financial institutions are adopting the Ripple network for ‘advantageous’ payment settlements and DeFi applications. The CTO explained why banks should prefer XRP over other on-chain networks like Ethereum, Solana, and others, given Ripple Ledger’s built-in design. He said financial institutions worldwide are increasingly adopting XRP infrastructure developed by Ripple Labs because of the network’s fast, low-cost cross-border transactions, high liquidity, robust on-chain applications, and transparency. These extraordinary attributes make Schwartz convinced that XRP has the upper hand over rivals. This explains why he believes banks should use XRP for payment and on-chain applications. He mentioned that XRP offers supersonic transaction speeds, with transaction times of 3-5 seconds and extremely low transaction fees. This is in sharp contrast to Ethereum which executes slow transactions and has higher transaction fees. While both Solana and XRP support high throughput and offer fast, low-cost transactions, the two networks are designed to address very different problems. XRP operates as an institutional payment network, specializing in the $150+ trillion cross-border settlement market through banking partnerships and regulatory clarity. On the other hand, Solana functions as a decentralized application network, built to power the emerging gaming, NFT, and DeFi economies through high speed and developer flexibility. Schwartz explains why XRP is different In the interview, Schwartz admitted that Solana and Ethereum each have unique advantages. He explained what XRP offers, including institutional adoption, cost efficiency, and speed. Based on his statement, these make XRP a better choice for banking, cross-border transactions, and international payment solutions. XRP has witnessed massive adoption among prominent financial companies like MoneyGram, American Express, Santander, and several other global banks. This suggests XRP has strong potential to be adopted by other banks worldwide to power their global payment systems.

Data.title: Thinking About Panic-selling XRP? Expert Says Read This First
Data.body: X Finance Bull has urged XRP holders to look beyond short-term price movements and examine the financial infrastructure being developed around tokenization, custody, settlement and institutional markets. In a lengthy post on X , the crypto commentator connected recent regulatory developments in the United States with Ripple’s expanding financial services and the capabilities being developed on the XRP Ledger. The post notes that the institutional market being built today could create a broader role for XRP and XRPL if tokenized assets become a larger part of global finance. Thinking about panic-selling $XRP ? Read this first. The SEC is building its 2027 examination program around tokenization, digital custody and modern market infrastructure, while Ripple is already expanding into those same financial functions. This is a long one. But I think… https://t.co/SxTRCzDocg pic.twitter.com/UOeYlvdwfE — X Finance Bull (@Xfinancebull) October 24, 2026 SEC Tokenization Priorities Draw Attention X Finance Bull began by asking readers to consider what a large U.S. investment manager would require to enter tokenized finance. The post listed regulatory clarity, custody, brokerage, settlement, liquidity, financing, ownership records and controlled market access among the necessary components. The commentator then connected those requirements to recent developments involving the SEC and Ripple. According to the post, the SEC’s 2027 examination priorities place tokenization, clearing infrastructure and emerging financial technology within its oversight plans. X Finance Bull noted that this indicates tokenized finance is moving into the regular supervision of U.S. capital markets rather than remaining a niche area of digital assets. The post also referenced the SEC’s March 17, 2026 interpretation, which it says identified XRP as an example of a digital commodity . X Finance Bull argued that this distinction allows XRP to exist as a digital commodity while tokenized securities remain subject to securities regulation. Ripple’s Institutional Expansion X Finance Bull then turned to Ripple’s growing presence across financial markets. The post cited Ripple Prime, formerly Hidden Road, and its regulated brokerage and clearing operations as examples of Ripple operating within established financial infrastructure. The commentator also discussed Ripple’s relationships with institutions including DTCC, Standard Chartered, DriveWealth, CSD BR, Meritz Securities and Brevan Howard. The post placed particular emphasis on tokenization. It cited DTCC’s work toward tokenized securities infrastructure and Ripple Prime’s participation in the DTCC Tokenization Service Industry Working Group. X Finance Bull also pointed to CSD BR’s partnership involving the representation and verification of selected BTG Pactual investment-fund records on XRPL using the Multi-Purpose Token standard. XRPL Features Could Support Regulated Markets The commentator argued that XRPL contains several features that could support institutional applications. These include Credentials, Permissioned Domains, Permissioned DEX functionality, Multi-Purpose Tokens, Token Escrow, freeze and clawback controls, and the ledger’s permanent transaction history. X Finance Bull said these capabilities address practical questions financial institutions must answer, including who can participate, who can transfer an asset and how ownership records can be verified. The post also highlighted RLUSD and institutional custody developments involving Standard Chartered, as well as DriveWealth’s planned use of RLUSD for settlement on XRPL. According to the commentator, these developments could place XRPL closer to actual brokerage, custody and settlement activity as tokenized financial products expand. Liquidity Remains the Core XRP Thesis X Finance Bull ultimately separated the broader Ripple and XRPL infrastructure discussion from the question of XRP’s own economic role. The commentator acknowledged XRP’s transaction fees and reserve requirements but identified liquidity as the more important long-term factor. The post argued that as tokenized dollars, securities, funds, bonds and other assets enter digital markets, institutions could require efficient ways to move between different assets and currencies. The post specifically referenced XRPL’s auto-bridging functionality and noted that XRP could become useful as an intermediary asset when it provides efficient execution between different markets. X Finance Bull stressed that this thesis does not depend on every institution adopting XRP. Instead, the commentator said the key consideration is whether recurring institutional flows eventually create sustained demand for XRP liquidity. Data.title: How one of our clients approached estate planning and opened a Kraken account in their trust’s name
Data.body: TL;DR One family set up a revocable trust , pour-over wills , a guardian and conservator nomination , and powers of attorney with an estate planning attorney. A trust only controls assets titled in its name , so retitling accounts takes real time and effort. The family opened a Kraken account in the trust’s name using trust documentation , trustee identification , and a taxpayer identification number . This is one family’s experience, not advice. Talk to a qualified estate planning attorney and tax adviser . Setting up a trust is rarely quick or comfortable. There’s paperwork, but mostly there are people: who you’d trust, who you’d ask, and what you’d want them to know. Below, one of our clients shares how their family approached it, from the first conversation with an attorney to opening a Kraken account in the trust’s name. It’s one family’s experience, in their words. It isn’t advice, and every situation is different, but if you’re considering something similar, it’s a useful look at what the process involved. Important: This article describes one Kraken client’s personal experience. It is not legal, tax, financial, or estate planning advice, and Kraken does not provide it. Estate and trust laws vary by state and country, and individual circumstances differ. Speak with a qualified estate planning attorney and tax adviser before making decisions. Why we started at 40 We turned 40 and started to feel old. More to the point, we started worrying about what would happen to our child, then 10, if we were not around. We live in Massachusetts, so we asked an estate planning attorney there for advice. We also figured the plan would be worth having even if we live another 40 years. It will still do its job when our child is an adult. What we set up On our attorney’s advice, we created a revocable trust. “Revocable” means we can change or cancel it during our lifetimes. The package included: A revocable trust, with my husband and me as the trustees (the people who manage the trust’s assets). A “pour-over” will for each of us. A pour-over will directs any assets left outside the trust at death into the trust. A nomination of a guardian and a conservator for our child. The guardian cares for a minor child; a conservator manages a minor’s money and property. A power of attorney for each of us, which lets a named person handle financial matters if we cannot. A health care proxy for each of us, which names someone to make medical decisions if we cannot. What our attorney said the trust was for Our attorney explained two main purposes. The first was to avoid probate, the court-supervised process for settling a person’s estate. The second was to manage assets for our child: the trust provides that a trustee manages the assets until she turns 25. One more point on taxes. A revocable trust, by itself, did not reduce our estate taxes. Federal and Massachusetts estate tax rules apply separately, and whether they matter depends on your circumstances. That is a question for your own attorney and tax adviser. The hardest part: choosing who would serve If both of us die, the trust’s successor trustee is my husband’s brother. If that person is unable to serve, a close friend from law school steps in. We left out my brother, who didn’t make the cut on responsibility. Deciding was hard. Telling these people, asking whether they were willing to serve, and getting their agreement was harder. We had several interviews with the law firm before we were done. A message to our child Our attorney also had us record a message to our daughter, to be shared if we were gone. It felt strange and, oddly, satisfying. We told her what we wanted her to know about us. We said that reading matters to us, and that we do not expect her to be perfect, only to pursue a life that has meaning to her. Moving our assets into the trust A trust only controls what is titled in its name, so we retitled everything: our bank accounts, our house, and our brokerage accounts. It was tedious, and it is the part of the process I would warn others about: lots of letters to banks and brokerages, providing the trust documents, etc. Opening a Kraken account in the trust’s name Our Kraken account was opened in the name of the trust from the start. We found it easy. Kraken’s standard onboarding flow for legal entities also handles trusts. We provided: The trust documentation. Identification for both trustees. A taxpayer identification number. Because ours is a revocable trust, this was one of our own numbers. Your situation may differ, so ask your attorney or tax adviser. Kraken reviewed the documents quickly, and the account was approved within hours, not days. Timing will vary for each client and is not guaranteed. That was not my experience elsewhere. When I tried to open accounts in the trust’s name at other major US exchanges, the applications sat in onboarding review for days, because they did not seem to know what to do with a trust. In my experience, Kraken’s support team handling this well was a real difference. Cost and time Legal fees were about $7,000, and the work took about a month. Fees vary widely by attorney, location, and complexity. Takeaways from one client These are our personal observations, not recommendations: Start with an estate planning attorney in your state. Rules vary across US states and other countries. Expect the decisions about people, not the paperwork, to take the most thought. A trust only works for assets titled in it, so plan time to retitle accounts. Before opening any account in a trust’s name, check what the trust documents and your attorney say about who may act for the trust. The right structure depends on where you live, what you own, and what you want to protect. That conversation belongs with your estate planning attorney and tax adviser. Opening the account in the trust’s name meant my crypto and equities holdings at Kraken sit inside the same plan as everything else we own. Today, my husband and I manage it as trustees. If something happens to us, our attorney explained that the successor trustees named in the trust, rather than a probate court, would be responsible for managing our assets for our daughter until she turns 25. For me, the real benefit is peace of mind. If we die, my daughter (who is now 16) and the trustee can go to one place to figure out where our assets are – a big binder with the trust and all the other documents and a list of our accounts (which are held by the trust). Data.title: GMO Internet says it will not pay hackers $50 million after server breach
Data.body: Group CEO Masatoshi Kumagai wrote on Oct. 26 that GMO Internet spurned a $50 million demand from hackers who broke into its Onamae.com Desktop Cloud service. As many as 26,739 servers may be affected and some customers said they saw unauthorized trades made through their brokerage accounts. Up to 26,739 Onamae.com servers may be affected Onamae.com Desktop Cloud runs brokerage software like MetaTrader 4 and MetaTrader 5 on customer servers. GMO said an attacker exploited a security flaw, planted malware in some customer environments and took customer data. The issue was first reported by a customer question on October 19. The following day, malware was detected and GMO began to shut down all plans from 19:00 UTC on October 20. The figure of 26,739 is a count of potentially impacted servers, not verified breaches. Some customers reported trades placed without permission via tools running on the service. In-house white-hat hackers had flagged security issues with the service in advance. The response was lacking in depth and speed, Kumagai wrote, and the attacker passed through the gap. GMO Internet Group shares shed almost 16% to a four-month low Monday. The company said it could not yet quantify the impact on earnings of the goodwill payments and compensation for losses. Attacker threatened accounts at over 70 securities and FX firms Kumagai’s blog post, first published Oct. 25 and updated a day later, lists what the attacker threatened. The list begins with more fraudulent orders on customer accounts at more than 70 securities and foreign-exchange firms in Japan and abroad. The attacker also threatened to leak data from customer PCs that were connected, use ransomware and publish internal details of GMO’s systems. Those were threats, not confirmed activity at all 70-plus firms. A document stamped 11:57 on October 21 demanded $50 million, about 8 billion yen. None of the demands were met by GMO and nothing was paid, Kumagai wrote. The note asked for payment in Bitcoin or Ether by 5 p.m. Japan time that day and said GMO’s crypto exchange subsidiary could pay immediately. Part of the attacker’s demand, as published by GMO Internet Group CEO Masatoshi Kumagai on his blog on October 26, 2026. GMO stated that paying would not guarantee the stolen data would not be misused. It is working with police and other authorities on the matter. Kumagai dismissed criticism that a flat 5,000 yen goodwill payment to all customers was an attempt to close the issue. It was the first step, he said. GMO Internet will verify and compensate for fraudulent trade losses related to the breach. If an exchange refuses a refund, it pays the full amount of eligible losses itself. The group also pledged a six-month free replacement environment, a reconstruction of its system base and an outside review of the root cause. GMO Cyber Security by Ierae and GMO Flatt Security are involved in defense and log analysis with approximately 200 security staff, including former Interpol personnel. GMO has also begun court disclosure requests to track down the attackers. Kumagai called the attack a symbol of an “AI cyber saturation attack,” with inexpensive AI tools that enable attackers to overpower defenders. GMO Cyber Security by Ierae found the autonomous AI penetration-testing tool ARTEX, built for defense, misused in attacks on some 20 Japanese companies. He also mentioned the recent PHP flaws where automated attack attempts ran to millions in hours. According to Cryptopolitan , the two PHP2Shell bugs have a severity score of 9.2 out of 10 and PHP shipped fixes on October 21. GMO has not connected its own breach to the PHP flaws . On Oct. 24, Kumagai asked Tokyo to apply Japan’s law on active cyber defense, which went into effect Oct. 1. GMO is not a designated critical-infrastructure operator under the law, and he acknowledged that the decision lies with the government. Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi said Monday evening the government plans an emergency package of cybersecurity safeguards by sometime next week. If you're reading this, you’re already ahead. Stay there with our newsletter .

Global asset management company Franklin Templeton is expected to launch two ETFs that redirect dividend income from investments in US equities to Bitcoin. The new products offer a different investment model between traditional financial markets and crypto assets. Dividend Income to be Directed Towards Bitcoin! According to documents Franklin Templeton submitted to the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC), the funds’ core strategy is based on investing in shares of U.S. companies and converting the dividends from these shares into Bitcoin investments. The planned funds include the Franklin US Equity Bitcoin DRIP Index ETF, which is based on an index covering the top 500 large-scale companies in the US. The Franklin US Innovation Bitcoin DRIP Index ETF, on the other hand, follows a different index that focuses on innovation-oriented companies. According to the statement, the initial target allocation for the funds is set at 95% stocks and 5% Bitcoin. Regular and special dividends from stocks are directed to Bitcoin according to specified rules. This aims to expose investors to the cryptocurrency through the fund without requiring them to purchase Bitcoin separately. ETF analyst Nate Geraci described the product, designed by Franklin Templeton, as “a smart product and an easy way for everyday investors to gain exposure to BTC.” He also added that this product could offer individual investors easy access to Bitcoin without having to buy the asset separately. *This is not investment advice.
